title: A Radio Segment on Workplace Burnout
script: Radio Host: [warmly] Good morning, listeners! Today we're talking about workplace burnout. We have a caller on the line. Hello there!
Caller: Hello! Thank you for taking my call this morning.
Radio Host: [honestly] Of course! What made you want to call in about this topic today?
Caller: Honestly, I've been working overtime for almost six months straight, and I finally reached my limit last week.
Radio Host: [thoughtful] I'm sorry to hear that. What happened exactly, if you don't mind sharing?
Caller: I sat at my desk on Monday and just couldn't focus on anything. I felt completely empty, not just tired.
Radio Host: [carefully] Did you know what the continuing tiredness and poor focus meant?
Caller: No. I avoided diagnosing myself and later arranged appropriate health support when the symptoms continued.
Radio Host: [reflective] What did you finally decide to do about it?
Caller: I spoke with my manager and asked for two days off, just to rest without checking any messages at all.
Radio Host: [practically] How did your manager respond to that request?
Caller: Much better than I expected. She said she had noticed I looked tired for weeks already.
Radio Host: [calmly] That must have been a relief, hearing that she already saw the signs.
Caller: It was. I think I hid it well, but apparently not as well as I believed.
Radio Host: [encouraging] What did those two days off actually look like for you?
Caller: I slept a lot, cooked simple meals, and went for short walks without my phone in my pocket.
Radio Host: Did it fully solve the problem, or was it just a small pause?
Caller: [warmly] Just a pause. I also discussed workload changes and knew I should seek qualified health care if the symptoms continued or became severe.
Radio Host: What limits have you set since coming back to work?
Caller: I stop answering messages after seven in the evening, and I take my full lunch break every single day.
Radio Host: [pleasantly] That sounds like real progress. Thank you so much for sharing your story with us this morning.
Caller: Thank you for listening. I hope someone out there recognizes these signs a little earlier than I did.
